narrative: Material PL1__MFDEA656 exhibits smooth daily demand averaging 4,185 units with no detectable trend over the analysis period. However, lead times are highly unstable (CV=68%), with a bimodal distribution spanning 0.7 to 5.2 days, which drives significant buffer requirements. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-based order quantity of 7,720 units is recommended, anchored by a safety stock of 7,607 units — 80x higher than the current SAP setting of 95 — to achieve the 95% service level target. Capacity utilisation remains at 34% post-replenishment, well within the 45,030 unit storage limit.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock (95) is critically insufficient; recommended safety stock is 7607 units
Lead time CV of 67.9% classifies as unstable; bimodal distribution detected in lead times

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) Continuous Review with Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: The smooth demand regime (CV=34.9%) with high-volume daily throughput and no trend makes a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. Fixed EOQ-based replenishment minimises total ordering and holding costs, while the reorder point directly absorbs the unstable lead-time risk via the sigma_ltd buffer.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (34% utilisation post-replenishment). MOQ of 1,645 is fully satisfied by the EOQ of 7,720. No capacity-driven constraints apply.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None. However, the 80x gap between current and recommended safety stock warrants urgent SAP master data review and supply chain risk assessment for the bimodal lead-time behaviour.
